svg.title: YouTube Video Ingestion & DAG Transcoding Architecture
svg.desc: End-to-end architecture of YouTube video processing: chunked resumable pre-signed upload, GOP-aligned preprocessor, DAG task graph, 3-queue Resource Manager, stateless hardware-accelerated worker pool, CMAF packaging, and multi-tier edge CDN delivery.
svg.text: YouTube Video Ingestion & DAG Transcoding Pipeline
Chunked Pre-Signed Upload · GOP Keyframe Slicing · 3-Queue Resource Manager · Stateless Encoders · Multi-Tier CDN Delivery
1. Pulls top task from Task Q
Master videos are sliced at keyframe I-frames into 2-4s GOPs.
If a worker crashes, only that single GOP chunk is retried,
not the full master file. Prevents cascading stalls and
enables massive parallel fan-out across stateless workers.
Key Benefit: Near-linear speedup with worker cluster scale.
Worker Queue routes compute by hardware (Argos VCU vs CPU).
Running Queue tracks leases; worker death triggers rapid
task re-queueing without zombie hangs or head-of-line stalls.
Key Benefit: Optimal VCU/GPU utilization and zero deadlock.
Raw cloud egress at $0.02/GB on 7.5 PB/day equals $150,000/day!
Deploying ISP-embedded caches (GGC and Netflix Open Connect)
pre-warms top 1% titles, absorbing > 95% of prime-time traffic
over zero-cost local ISP peering links directly to viewers.
Key Benefit: Slashes multi-million-dollar WAN transit bills.
